hitPoints.atHigherLevels: 1d12 (or 7) + your Constitution modifier per barbarian level after 1st

features.name: Rage
features.description: In battle, you fight with primal ferocity. On your turn, you can enter a rage as a bonus action...

effects.condition: while raging (and not in heavy armor)

features.name: Unarmored Defense
features.description: While you are not wearing any armor, your Armor Class equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Constitution modifier. You can use a shield and still gain this benefit.

features.name: Reckless Attack
features.description: You can throw aside all concern for defense to attack with fierce desperation...

features.name: Danger Sense
features.description: You have advantage on Dexterity saving throws against effects that you can see, such as traps and spells, as long as you aren’t blinded, deafened, or incapacitated.

features.name: Primal Path
features.description: You choose a path that shapes the nature of your rage. Choose Path of the Berserker or Path of the Totem Warrior (PHB).

features.name: Extra Attack
features.description: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

features.name: Fast Movement
features.description: Your speed increases by 10 feet while you aren’t wearing heavy armor.

features.name: Feral Instinct
features.description: Your instincts are so honed that you have advantage on initiative rolls.

features.name: Brutal Critical
features.description: You can roll one additional weapon damage die when determining the extra damage for a critical hit with a melee attack. This increases to two additional dice at 13th level and three at 17th level.

features.name: Relentless Rage
features.description: Your rage can keep you fighting despite grievous wounds. If you drop to 0 hit points while raging and don’t die outright, you can make a CON save (DC 10, +5 each subsequent time) to drop to 1 hit point instead.

features.name: Persistent Rage
features.description: Your rage is so fierce that it ends early only if you fall unconscious or if you choose to end it.

features.name: Indomitable Might
features.description: If your total for a Strength check is less than your Strength score, you can use that score in place of the total.

features.name: Primal Champion
features.description: You embody the power of the wilds. Your Strength and Constitution scores increase by 4. Your maximum for those scores is now 24.

subclasses.name: Path of the Berserker
subclasses.description: For some barbarians, rage is a means to an end—that end being violence...

features.name: Frenzy
features.description: Starting when you choose this path at 3rd level, you can go into a frenzy when you rage. If you do so, for the duration of your rage you can make a single melee weapon attack as a bonus action on each of your turns after this one. When your rage ends, you suffer one level of exhaustion.

effects.condition: while raging (after the turn you enter rage)

features.name: Mindless Rage
features.description: Beginning at 6th level, you can’t be charmed or frightened while raging. If you are charmed or frightened when you enter your rage, the effect is suspended for the duration of the rage.

features.name: Intimidating Presence
features.description: Beginning at 10th level, you can use your action to frighten someone with your menacing presence. Choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of you. If it can see or hear you, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier) or be frightened of you until the end of your next turn. On subsequent turns, you can use your action to extend the duration on that creature. The effect ends if it ends its turn out of your line of sight or more than 60 feet away. If it succeeds on its saving throw, you can’t use this feature on that creature again for 24 hours.

effects.duration: until end of your next turn

features.name: Retaliation
features.description: Starting at 14th level, when you take damage from a creature that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against that creature.

subclasses.name: Path of the Totem Warrior
subclasses.description: The Path of the Totem Warrior is a spiritual journey...

features.name: Spirit Seeker
features.description: You gain the ability to cast beast sense and speak with animals as rituals.

hitPoints.atHigherLevels: 1d8 (or 5) + your Constitution modifier per cleric level after 1st

options.description: A shield and a holy symbol

features.name: Spellcasting
features.description: You have learned to draw on divine magic through meditation and prayer. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability; you prepare a number of cleric spells equal to your Wisdom modifier + your cleric level (minimum of one spell).

features.name: Divine Domain
features.description: Choose a divine domain that shapes your practice of cleric magic. Your choice grants you features at 1st level and again at 2nd, 6th, 8th, and 17th level.

features.name: Channel Divinity
features.description: You can channel divine energy to fuel magical effects. You start with one use of Channel Divinity. You regain expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.

features.name: Turn Undead
features.description: As an action, you present your holy symbol and speak a prayer censuring the undead. Each undead that can see or hear you within 30 feet must make a Wisdom saving throw. If the creature fails its saving throw, it is turned for 1 minute or until it takes damage.

features.name: Destroy Undead
features.description: When an undead fails its saving throw against your Turn Undead feature, the creature is instantly destroyed if its challenge rating is at or below a certain threshold (CR 1/2 at 5th, CR 1 at 8th, CR 2 at 11th, CR 3 at 14th).

features.name: Divine Intervention
features.description: You can call on your deity to intervene on your behalf when your need is great. Roll percentile dice; if the roll is equal to or less than your cleric level, your deity intervenes. If successful, you can’t use this feature again for 7 days.

features.name: Improved Divine Intervention
features.description: Your call for intervention succeeds automatically, no roll required.

subclasses.name: Life Domain
subclasses.description: The Life domain focuses on vibrancy, health, and healing. Clerics of this domain are guardians of life and vitality.

features.name: Bonus Proficiency
features.description: You gain proficiency with heavy armor.

features.name: Disciple of Life
features.description: Your healing spells are more effective. Whenever you use a spell of 1st level or higher to restore hit points to a creature, the creature regains additional hit points equal to 2 + the spell’s level.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Preserve Life
features.description: You can use Channel Divinity to heal a number of hit points equal to five times your cleric level, divided among any creatures within 30 feet of you.

features.name: Blessed Healer
features.description: When you cast a spell of 1st level or higher that restores hit points to a creature other than you, you also regain hit points equal to 2 + the spell’s level.

features.name: Divine Strike
features.description: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 radiant damage. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

features.name: Supreme Healing
features.description: When you would normally roll one or more dice to restore hit points with a spell, you instead use the highest number possible for each die.

hitPoints.atHigherLevels: 1d8 (or 5) + your Constitution modifier per rogue level after 1st

options.description: A shortbow and a quiver of 20 arrows

features.name: Expertise
features.description: Choose two of your skill proficiencies (or one skill and your proficiency with thieves’ tools). Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of the chosen proficiencies.

features.name: Sneak Attack
features.description: You know how to strike subtly and exploit a foe’s distraction. Once per turn, you can deal extra damage to one creature you hit with an attack if you have advantage on the attack roll or meet the other conditions.

features.name: Thieves’ Cant
features.description: You have learned thieves’ cant, a secret mix of dialect, jargon, and code that allows you to hide messages in seemingly normal conversation.

features.name: Cunning Action
features.description: Your quick thinking and agility allow you to move and act quickly. You can take the Dash, Disengage, or Hide action as a bonus action on each of your turns.

features.name: Roguish Archetype
features.description: You choose an archetype that you emulate in your roguish techniques (e.g., Thief).

features.name: Uncanny Dodge
features.description: When an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to halve the attack’s damage against you.

effects.condition: when hit by an attacker you can see

features.name: Evasion
features.description: You can nimbly dodge out of the way of certain area effects; you take no damage on a successful DEX save, and only half damage on a failed save.

features.name: Reliable Talent
features.description: Whenever you make an ability check that lets you add your proficiency bonus, you can treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

features.name: Blindsense
features.description: If you are able to hear, you are aware of the location of any hidden or invisible creature within 10 feet of you.

features.name: Slippery Mind
features.description: You gain proficiency in Wisdom saving throws.

features.name: Elusive
features.description: No attack roll has advantage against you while you aren’t incapacitated.

features.name: Stroke of Luck
features.description: If your attack misses a target within range, you can turn the miss into a hit. Alternatively, if you fail an ability check, you can treat the d20 roll as a 20 (1/short or long rest).

subclasses.name: Thief
subclasses.description: Thieves are fast and agile, focusing on stealth, agility, and exploiting opportunities.

features.name: Fast Hands
features.description: You can use the bonus action granted by your Cunning Action to make a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check, use your thieves’ tools to disarm a trap or open a lock, or take the Use an Object action.

features.name: Second-Story Work
features.description: You gain the ability to climb faster than normal; climbing no longer costs you extra movement, and when you make a running jump, the distance you cover increases by a number of feet equal to your DEX modifier.

features.name: Supreme Sneak
features.description: You have advantage on a Dexterity (Stealth) check if you move no more than half your speed on the same turn.

features.name: Use Magic Device
features.description: You can attune to any magic item and ignore all class, race, and level requirements on the use of magic items.

features.name: Thief’s Reflexes
features.description: You can take two turns during the first round of any combat; you take your first turn at your initiative and your second at your initiative minus 10.

hitPoints.atHigherLevels: 1d6 (or 4) + your Constitution modifier per wizard level after 1st

features.name: Spellcasting
features.description: You have a spellbook containing spells that show the first glimmerings of your true power. INT is your spellcasting ability; you can cast rituals and prepare a list of wizard spells each day.

features.name: Arcane Recovery
features.description: Once per day when you finish a short rest, you can choose expended spell slots to recover. The spell slots can have a combined level that is equal to or less than half your wizard level (rounded up), and none of the slots can be 6th level or higher.

features.name: Arcane Tradition
features.description: You choose an arcane tradition, shaping your practice of magic (e.g., School of Evocation).

features.name: Spell Mastery
features.description: You have achieved such mastery over certain spells that you can cast them at will. Choose a 1st-level and a 2nd-level wizard spell you can cast without expending a spell slot (with restrictions).

features.name: Signature Spells
features.description: You gain two 3rd-level wizard spells as signature spells. You always have these spells prepared, they don’t count against the number of spells you can prepare, and you can cast each of them once at 3rd level without expending a spell slot.

subclasses.name: School of Evocation
subclasses.description: You focus your study on magic that creates powerful elemental effects and blasts of energy.

features.name: Evocation Savant
features.description: The gold and time you must spend to copy an evocation spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Sculpt Spells
features.description: You can create pockets of relative safety within the effects of your evocation spells to protect allies.

features.name: Potent Cantrip
features.description: Your damaging cantrips affect even creatures that avoid the brunt of the effect; they take half damage on a successful save (if applicable).

features.name: Empowered Evocation
features.description: You can add your INT modifier to one damage roll of any wizard evocation spell you cast.

features.name: Overchannel
features.description: You can maximize damage of a 1st–5th level spell you cast; subsequent uses before a long rest deal increasing necrotic damage to you.

hitPoints.atHigherLevels: 1d10 (or 6) + your Constitution modifier per paladin level after 1st

options.description: A martial weapon and a shield
Chain mail and a holy symbol
Scale mail and a holy symbol (if preferred by table rules)

features.name: Divine Sense
features.description: As an action, open your awareness to detect celestials, fiends, and undead, and areas consecrated or desecrated.

effects.duration: until end of your next turn

features.name: Lay on Hands
features.description: Pool of healing equal to 5 × your paladin level that you can use to restore hit points or cure diseases/poisons.

features.name: Fighting Style
features.description: You adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty (Defense, Dueling, Great Weapon Fighting, Protection).

features.name: Spellcasting
features.description: You can cast paladin spells. Charisma is your spellcasting ability. You prepare a number of paladin spells equal to your Charisma modifier + half your paladin level (minimum one).

features.name: Divine Smite
features.description: When you hit with a melee weapon attack, you can expend a spell slot to deal radiant damage in addition to the weapon’s damage.

features.name: Divine Health
features.description: Your divine magic makes you immune to disease.

features.name: Sacred Oath
features.description: You swear a sacred oath that grants you features at 3rd, 7th, 15th, and 20th level.

features.name: Extra Attack
features.description: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

features.name: Aura of Protection
features.description: While you are conscious, you and friendly creatures within range gain a bonus to saving throws equal to your Charisma modifier.

features.name: Aura of Courage
features.description: You and friendly creatures within range can’t be frightened while you are conscious.

features.name: Improved Divine Smite
features.description: Your melee weapon attacks deal an extra 1d8 radiant damage.

features.name: Cleansing Touch
features.description: You can end one spell on yourself or on one willing creature that you touch a number of times per long rest equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum once).

subclasses.name: Oath of Devotion
subclasses.description: Paladins of Devotion uphold the highest ideals of justice, virtue, and order.

features.name: Channel Divinity (Devotion)
features.description: You gain Sacred Weapon and Turn the Unholy options for Channel Divinity.

features.name: Aura of Devotion
features.description: You and friendly creatures within your aura can’t be charmed while you are conscious.

features.name: Purity of Spirit
features.description: You are always under the effects of protection from evil and good.

features.name: Holy Nimbus
features.description: As an action, you can emanate holy light that harms foes and brightens the area for 1 minute (once per long rest).

hitPoints.atHigherLevels: 1d10 (or 6) + your Constitution modifier per fighter level after 1st

options.description: A martial weapon and a shield

features.name: Fighting Style
features.description: You adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty (Archery, Defense, Dueling, Great Weapon Fighting, Protection, Two-Weapon Fighting).

features.name: Second Wind
features.description: You have a limited well of stamina; as a bonus action, you can regain hit points equal to 1d10 + your fighter level (1/short or long rest).

features.name: Action Surge
features.description: On your turn, you can take one additional action on top of your regular action and a possible bonus action (1/short or long rest; 2 uses at 17th).

features.name: Martial Archetype
features.description: You choose an archetype that you strive to emulate in your combat styles and techniques (e.g., Champion).

features.name: Extra Attack
features.description: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn (three attacks at 11th level, four at 20th).

features.name: Indomitable
features.description: You can reroll a saving throw that you fail (1/long rest; 2 uses at 13th; 3 uses at 17th).

subclasses.name: Champion
subclasses.description: The Champion focuses on the development of raw physical power honed to deadly perfection.

features.name: Improved Critical
features.description: Your weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20.

features.name: Remarkable Athlete
features.description: Add half your proficiency bonus (round up) to any Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution check you make that doesn’t already use your proficiency bonus; your long jump distance increases by a number of feet equal to your Strength modifier.

features.name: Additional Fighting Style
features.description: You can choose a second option from the Fighting Style feature.

features.name: Superior Critical
features.description: Your weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 18–20.

features.name: Survivor
features.description: You regain hit points at the start of each of your turns equal to 5 + your Constitution modifier if you have no more than half of your hit points left and you aren’t at 0 hit points.
